heatRecordsLink.what: Opens the temperature records database (Operations > Temperatures), where these readings come from: each reading with who took it, the time, the photo and which sensor or refrigerator it comes from. It only shows if you have that screen in your access.
heatRecordsLink.example: you see a zone in red at 14:00, tap the link and check there the photo and who captured that reading.

heatDay.what: The day whose climate you want to see. Readings are stored in UTC and shown here in your time. It starts on today.
heatDay.example: you choose November 3 to see how the warehouse warmed up that day.

heatMetric.what: What is painted on the map: Temperature (°C, 0 to 40) or Humidity (%, 0 to 100). The scale is fixed so one day can be compared with another. Single-type sensors (for example, humidity only) only appear in what they measure.
heatMetric.example: you tap Humidity and the zones are painted with the humidity their sensors showed.

heatPlay.what: Plays the day hour by hour to see how each zone warms up and cools down. It stops at the end of the day or when tapped again.
heatPlay.example: you start at 08:00 and the map changes color until 23:00.

heatHour.what: The hour you see on the map. The green dots below are the hours that have readings of what you are viewing. In each hour the last reading of each sensor is used.
heatHour.example: you drag to 14:00 and each zone shows the average of what its sensors showed at that hour.

heatModes.what: How what is painted is calculated. Specific hour: the hour you move on the bar (and Play the day steps the map hour by hour). From one hour to another: all readings between two times of the day. Whole day: all readings from 00:00 to 23:59.
heatModes.example: you pick From one hour to another, 08:00 to 14:00, and each zone is painted with what its sensors marked in that window.

heatValue.what: Which number paints each zone when you calculate a time window: the average of all readings, the lowest (minimum) or the highest (maximum). The list on the right always shows all three.
heatValue.example: you switch to maximum to see how hot each zone got during the day.

heatCalc.what: Calculates the time window you typed (From one hour to another) or the whole day. The map and the list fill with the result; if you change the hours, tap it again.
heatCalc.example: you change 08:00 to 10:00 and tap Calculate: the map is painted again.

heatMap.what: The cost center's Layout with each zone painted with the average of what its sensors showed at that hour (blue = cold, red = hot). Each circle is a sensor, with its own value. A gray zone with a dotted line has no sensors or no reading at that hour: no data is made up.
heatMap.example: the Refrigerated zone in blue with 5.6 °C, the Dock in orange with 34.4 °C and the Office in gray because it has no sensor.

heatZones.what: The list of zones with their value at the chosen hour: how many sensors the average comes from and what each one showed, at what time and who captured it.
heatZones.example: Zone 1 · 31.2 °C, average of S001 and S006; below, S001 31.8 °C at 14:10 by Ana.

layoutLock_codes.what: Lets whoever scans the Layout, Zone or Category QR search codes (by SKU, description or category) in the search box. Off, the search only finds zones, furniture and locations, and no code appears in the list.
layoutLock_codes.example: a visitor scans the warehouse QR and types “glove”: with the lock open they see the codes; with it off they only see the rack and the zone.

layoutLock_classifications.what: Lets people see the classifications of a category (Category QR) and the list of articles of each one. Off, the Category shows its name but no longer opens the classifications or their articles.
layoutLock_classifications.example: the Medicines category QR shows “Controlled”, “Generic”…; off, it only shows the category name.

layoutLock_photos.what: Lets people see the photos of the articles in the classification lists. Off, the articles show an icon instead of their photo.
layoutLock_photos.example: the “Generic” classification list shows the photo of each box; off, each article shows an icon.

layoutLock_where.what: Lets people see where each code is (the route Zone › Rack › Level) in the search and in the lists, and the racks painted on the map. Off, codes appear without their location.
layoutLock_where.example: “000412 · Nitrile glove M” shows “Zone 6 › A005 › Level 2”; off, it shows only the code and the name.

layoutLock_metrics.what: Lets people see the metric data: area, volume and the indicators per zone, with the measures and m² buttons on the map. Off, the page shows no figure in meters. Note: the drawing of the map stays the same.
layoutLock_metrics.example: the Layout page shows “Metric data · 4,200 m² of total area”; off, that block no longer appears.

layoutLock_doors.what: Lets people see the doors and the power connections on the map and in 3D. Off, the server no longer sends them and their layers disappear.
layoutLock_doors.example: the map draws the warehouse doors and power outlets; off, the warehouse shows without doors or power.

layoutLock_counts.what: Lets people see how many codes each zone, category and classification has. Off, those numbers are removed.
layoutLock_counts.example: “Zone 6 · 12 codes” and “Controlled 8”; off, only the name of the zone and of the classification remains.

layoutQrLocks.what: The locks decide what the person scanning a QR without a session sees and can do: see the previous records, their photos and the name of who made them, how many records are shown (3, 10 or 20), see the range and the alerts (Temperatures only) and allow registering (off = the QR is for viewing only). There is one setting per QR type and it applies to all of that type in this Layout, including the ones already printed; today everything is open. The locks are enforced by the server, not only by the page. You, with your user, still see everything on the Cleaning and Temperatures screens.
layoutQrLocks.example: you turn off “See the photos of the records” in Cleaning and whoever scans no longer sees photos in “View records”, even if the QR was printed months ago.

layoutRango.what: The refrigerator limits (Cold-type assets only): minimum and maximum temperature in °C and minimum and maximum humidity in %. Each one is optional (empty = no such limit). Temperature readings outside this range are flagged in red on the QR page when saved and in the records table (Status column). Each reading is judged with the range the refrigerator had when it was taken.
layoutRango.example: you set a medicine refrigerator to min. 2 and max. 8 °C: a reading of 10 °C is flagged as out of range.

layoutRenumerar.what: Renumbers the asset codes: in each zone and type they become consecutive from 001 (A001, A002… F001, F002…), in the order of their current number. Saved codes do not move on their own, which is why this is a button. It shows in the table and is applied when you save. QR codes, locators and code relations keep working because they use the asset, not its code; anything already printed with the old code will no longer match.
layoutRenumerar.example: the refrigerators ended up as F020 and F021: you touch Renumber codes and they become F001 and F002; you save the Layout.

colCapCodigo.what: The code (SKU) stored in this Layout location. When you choose it, the system takes its measures and stacking data to calculate how much fits. Filling it needs View and Operate; changing or removing it needs Modify (and your manager’s approval when it applies).
colCapCodigo.example: you choose code TBUL13244 for location A001: its UoM, stacking and capacity appear.

colCapHuellas.what: How many pallets of the code fit on the floor of this location. It counts what really fits on each side (a 2.5 × 2.5 m location with a 1 × 1 m pallet fits 4, not 6) and takes the layout, facing forward or turned, that fits the most.
colCapHuellas.example: a 22.4 × 2.6 m location with a 1.4 × 2.6 m pallet: 16 footprints.

colCapMaxima.what: The maximum capacity of the location in the code’s UoM: footprints × capacity per footprint. Capacity per footprint is max stacking × capacity per pallet (quantity per layer × layers per pallet). It is calculated on its own; if a code data point is missing it stays empty and the row says which one.

pmQr.what: Shows the Manual Order QR of the cost center selected above. Stick it in the warehouse: whoever scans it searches for the item (by code, description, unit of measure or category), enters the quantity and sends the order; it arrives here with their name and the time. The same window downloads the image and opens or closes the QR locks.
pmQr.example: you print the Main Warehouse QR and stick it by the door: staff request what they need from their phones.

pmEstatus.what: Where each order line is: Pending (just arrived) or Supplied (already delivered). Whoever has View and Operate on the Status column changes it here; every change is kept in the history.
pmEstatus.example: you deliver the 24 milk units: you change the line to Supplied.

layoutFind.what: Search a zone or a footprint, by its code or its name, and the map, the 3D view, the tables and the summary keep only what is inside it; the rest of the warehouse is hidden. The tables do not lose rows: the ones that are not part of the focus are just tucked away. It is screen-only: it changes nothing that is saved or printed.
layoutFind.example: you type “Zone 6” and pick the zone: the map zooms in and only its footprints and assets show; you type “H005” and only its assets show.

layoutFxTodo.what: Turns on all the options below to see the whole Layout at once. If they are all on already, it keeps only the one you are editing.
layoutFxTodo.example: you press All to see walls, doors, zones and assets together; you press it again to keep only the step you are editing.

layoutFxEnfocado.what: What you are focusing on: the zone or footprint you searched, or the asset, level or position of the row you chose. Press Hidden or Faded so the rest of the warehouse is removed or dimmed; press it again to leave it as it was, or press the X to remove the focus. The tables keep all their rows: only the drawing changes. With Faded the options that are off also show faded instead of being removed, and the assets you mark in Choose assets show up here (3 of 14 assets chosen): the others are removed (Hidden) or dimmed (Faded).
layoutFxEnfocado.example: you choose level 2 of rack A013 and press Faded: the 3D dims the whole warehouse and marks level 2 in orange.

layoutFindDonde.what: First step: where to search. «All» is the whole building. «Zones» shows the zones so you can tick one or several: the list, the «What to see» numbers, the sketch, the 3D view, the tables and the summary keep only what is inside or on the edge of those zones. It only changes what you see: it does not change what is saved.
layoutFindDonde.example: you tap Zones and tick Zone 6 and Reception: you only see and search what is in those two zones; you tap All and see the whole building again.

layoutFindZonas.what: The zones of the Layout. Tap one to tick or untick it; you can tick several. With at least one ticked, the sketch and the rest focus on them.
layoutFindZonas.example: you tick Zone 6 and Reception and the sketch zooms in on both; you untick Reception and only Zone 6 stays.

layoutFindTipos.what: Second step: what to see of what you chose in «Search in». All, or one or several types at once (zones, footprints, assets, walls, doors, floors, safety, sensors, power, obstacles, aisles or objects). The number on each type is how many match what you type and, with zones chosen, how many are inside them. Only the types of steps your account can see appear. With zones chosen, what you turn on is also drawn on the sketch; without zones it only filters the list. Picking a zone or a footprint from the list focuses it; picking anything else turns on its step, marks its row in the table and the sketch zooms in and highlights it.
layoutFindTipos.example: you choose Zone 6 and Reception and turn on Walls and Doors: the list and the sketch only bring the walls and doors of those two zones.

layout3dLayers.what: In 3D the layers follow the same steps as the map: when you turn a step on (Outline, Doors, Zones, Footprint-Space, Electrical Power, Assets) its layer is shown and when you turn it off it is hidden. The Layers list only has what does not have a step of its own: Walls and Columns, to hide them even if Outline is on. What you hide is no longer seen or touchable. The list is remembered in this browser.
layout3dLayers.example: you turn Zones on and the zones appear in 3D; you turn Zones off and they hide; to see the whole floor without obstacles, you remove the check on Walls in the Layers list.

layout3dViews.what: Places the 3D camera: Overview (diagonal), Top view (from above, like the sketch) or Front view (from the side, to see heights).
layout3dViews.example: to compare the racks' height with the walls', use Front view.

layout3dLabels.what: Shows or hides the 3D labels: each zone's name and each space's code.
layout3dLabels.example: if many spaces are close together and their codes overlap, hide them to see the shape better.

layout3dZoom.what: Zooms the 3D in or out. Also with Ctrl and the mouse wheel, or two fingers on a phone.
layout3dZoom.example: zoom in to see a rack up close and tap it to see its measures.

layout3dStage.what: The Layout in 3D. Drag to rotate, Shift or right click to move, Ctrl and wheel (or two fingers) to zoom. Tap an asset, a footprint or a zone to see its name, measures and levels; also, in the step you are editing (Zones, Footprint-Space or Assets) its row is marked in the table and scrolled into view, like when you tap it on the map.
layout3dStage.example: tap rack R-07 and below the drawing you get its type, zone, measures and how many levels it has.

layoutViews.what: The buttons to change how the Layout looks. At the top you choose 2D (the flat map) or 3D, and below only the options of the chosen view appear: in 2D, the Texts list (names, m² and measures), rotate and zoom; in 3D, the camera, the layers, which assets are shown, the labels and zoom. They only change what you see; they do not modify the Layout.
layoutViews.example: you switch to 3D, open Layers and hide the walls to see the whole floor; you go back to 2D and there you see the Texts list.

layoutTextos.what: A round button (Aa) that opens a list, floating on top of everything else, to show or hide the texts of the drawing. In 2D: the zone names, the m² of each zone and the side measures; in 3D: the labels. Each row with a check mark is visible; tap it to hide it and tap it again to show it. You only see the rows you have in the tree. It is remembered in this browser and the sheet you download comes out as you see it.
layoutTextos.example: you open Texts, remove the check on "Side measures" and the map is left with just the zone names and m².

layoutLocalizadores.what: The Locators step: when you tap it the list of the locators this Layout is creating appears below (one per zone, footprint, asset and complete position), view-only. The arrow next to it takes you straight to the Catalogs > Locators screen, with all the cost centers. It only shows if you have that screen in the tree.
layoutLocalizadores.example: you tap Locators and see the list of this Layout; you tap the arrow and the full screen opens.

layoutSec_localizadores.what: The locators this Layout is creating, complete or partial, with what you have entered right now (also what is not saved yet): one per zone, per footprint, per asset and per complete 7-piece position. It is view-only: a locator is changed in the other steps. The arrow next to the name opens the Locators screen, with all the cost centers, the warehouse and the sub-warehouse.
layoutSec_localizadores.example: you finish placing the racks of Zone 6, tap Locators and see the new locators right away; if you want the full screen, you tap the arrow.

layoutLocalizadoresLink.what: Opens the Catalogs > Locators screen (view-only) with all the locators of all the cost centers, their warehouse and sub-warehouse, filters and history. It is the quick access to go straight there, without the menu.
layoutLocalizadoresLink.example: you want to look up a locator of another cost center: you tap the arrow and filter there.

layoutActivoMedidas.what: The place and own measures of this asset inside its footprint, all optional: X and Y are the distance from the corner of the footprint; Length, Depth and Height are its measures. If you leave it empty, the asset places itself: it goes next to the other assets of its footprint, in the order of the table, against the edge, and with the measures of the footprint (the leftover length is shared among those without one). What it would take now shows in gray inside the box. An asset cannot go outside its footprint, be taller than it or overlap another: what does not fit is marked in red and cannot be saved.
layoutActivoMedidas.example: a 5 m footprint with three racks: the first gets Length 2, the second Length 1.5 and Depth 1.0, and the third is left empty: it takes the 1.5 m left and all of them go next to each other.

layoutQrSeguridad.what: Prints the safety QR codes: one per Layout element (fire extinguishers, hydrants, emergency doors, first-aid kits… the ones you marked in the Safety step), for the zone you choose or all of them. Each QR is stuck next to its element and, when scanned, whoever checks types their name, marks it OK or Faulty, may leave a note and takes the photo at that moment (the system sets the time). The checks are seen in Operations > Safety: an OK check moves the element's next check forward by itself and a Faulty one marks it that way until another comes out OK. The QR never changes, even if you move the element.
layoutQrSeguridad.example: you choose Zone 1 and the QR of E001 and I001 is printed; you stick them next to each one and whoever checks scans the extinguisher's, marks OK, writes "gauge in the green" and takes the photo.

layoutQrSensor.what: Prints the sensor QR codes: one per sensor of the Layout (the ones you marked in the Sensors step), for the zone you choose or all of them. Each QR is stuck next to its sensor and, when scanned, whoever checks writes their name and what the sensor shows (temperature, humidity or both, depending on its type) and takes a photo of the reading at that moment (the system sets the time). The readings are saved in the same Temperatures database and feed the heat map. The QR never changes, even if you move the sensor.
layoutQrSensor.example: you choose Zone 1 and the QR of S001 and S006 is printed; you stick them next to each sensor and whoever checks scans each one, writes 31.8 °C and 46 % and takes a photo of the display.

layoutQrTemp.what: Prints the temperature QR codes: one per refrigerator (the Cold-type assets), for the zone you choose or all of them. Each QR is stuck on its refrigerator and, when scanned, the person checking types their name and the temperature shown and takes the photo of the reading at that moment (the time is set by the system). The readings are seen in Operations > Temperatures. They can also be downloaded as a PDF (one card per page) or as an image, in the size you choose, like in the Layout.
layoutQrTemp.example: you choose Zone 2 and the QR of each refrigerator F001, F002… is printed; you stick them on and whoever checks scans each one, types 4.5 °C and takes the photo of the thermometer.

layoutQrClean.what: Prints the cleaning QR codes: one per asset (a rack, a cabinet, a pallet, a refrigerator…), of the zone you choose or of all of them. Each QR is stuck on its asset and, when scanned, whoever cleans opens the cleaning screen of THAT asset: types a name, takes the "before" photo with the camera and the timer starts; when finished takes the "after" photo. No user needed. The QR codes never change even if the asset changes name, zone or code. The records are seen in Operations > Cleaning. They can also be downloaded as a PDF (one card per page) or as an image, in the size you choose, like in the Layout.
layoutQrClean.example: you choose Zone 6 and all its racks are printed with their QR; you stick them and the cleaning staff scans each one.

layoutQrCls.what: Downloads the sheet with the classifications of an Inventory category (PDF or image), with their icon, color and one QR each. Each QR opens, in the chosen zone, the list of codes of that classification. It does not depend on codes: the QRs never change and scanning always shows what is current. Each category's classifications are linked in Our Inventory Categories.
layoutQrCls.example: you pick MEDICAMENTOS and Zone 1: the sheet comes out with Patent, Generic, Antibiotic…, each with its QR.

layoutQrZoneSheet.what: Downloads the zone sheet (PDF or image) with the list of categories, how many codes each has and one QR per category. The QRs never change: scanning one always shows what is current, even if the sheet was printed months ago. The list comes from what is saved in Code Relation.
layoutQrZoneSheet.example: you print the Zone 1 sheet on half letter and stick it at the zone entrance.

layoutFilterClear.what: Removes every filter from this table and shows all its rows again. Filters are set with the funnel in each header, like in the other tables.
layoutFilterClear.example: you filtered the Type column to see only aisles; when you are done, Clear filters brings back all the zones.

layoutZoneFmt.what: Opens this zone's format, like Excel's Format Cells: background color, stripes or pattern, and border style and color. Without its own format, the zone uses its type color.
layoutZoneFmt.example: you give the Warehouse purple diagonal stripes and a dashed border to tell it apart from other dry zones.

layoutFmtColor.what: Opens the system color window (the same one used in the trees) to pick this color; the change shows right away in the preview.
layoutFmtColor.example: you pick a light yellow background and an amber for the stripes.

layoutFmtPattern.what: Fill stripes or pattern: diagonal, horizontal, vertical, grid, dots or crossed stripes. Solid is one color and No fill shows what is underneath.
layoutFmtPattern.example: diagonal stripes to mark a zone under construction.

layoutFmtLine.what: Line style of the zone border: solid (thin, medium or thick), dashed, dotted, dash-dot, double or none.
layoutFmtLine.example: a dashed border for a temporary zone.

layoutFloorFmt.what: Choose the color, the pattern (stripes, dots, grid…) and the border of this floor. Without its own format the floor takes the color of its level: the ones that go up run from amber to red (higher, darker) and the pits are blue. You can apply it to this floor only or to all the floors at the same level. A floor at level (0) is not painted.
layoutFloorFmt.example: you set the +0.33 m floors to green stripes to tell them apart from the +0.60 m platform.

layoutAssetFmt.what: Changes the color, stripes and border of the asset (the rack, cabinet or pallet on top of the footprint), like in Zones and Footprint-Space. Without its own color the asset is sand-colored, different from the white of the footprint, so they can be told apart. In "Apply to" you choose whether the change is only for this asset, for those of its zone or for those of the same type. Color rule: what goes INSIDE something cannot have the color of what contains it (the asset cannot have the color of its footprint, nor the footprint that of its zone) because it gets confusing; the same color can be used elsewhere.
layoutAssetFmt.example: you paint the racks of Zone 6 blue with "Those of the same type"; if the footprint were already blue, the system asks you to choose a different blue.

layoutSpaceFmt.what: Opens the color window of this footprint (Fill and Border, with preview). Without its own format the footprint looks white; the small square next to the icon is the color it already has. It shows on the map, on the QR page, on the downloaded sheet and in the 3D view.
layoutSpaceFmt.example: you paint rack R-02 blue with stripes and its row shows a blue square.

layoutFmtScope.what: Which footprints get what you choose: only this one, the rest of its zone, or those of the same asset type (the one chosen in the Assets step). What the others already had is replaced. With its own format you can open the window and accept without changing anything to copy it to the rest of the group; Remove format also applies to the chosen group.
layoutFmtScope.example: you choose «Those of the same asset type» with type Rack and every rack gets the same color.

vfLocator.what: The complete Locator of this place, always with the 7 pieces: zone, footprint, asset, level, column, row and depth. It is the same one used in the Code Relation template and can be copied as it is.
vfLocator.example: Z006.H005.A005.N003.C001.F001.P001 is zone 6, footprint 5, asset A5, level 3, column 1, row 1 and depth 1.

relFootprint.what: The footprint (the place on the floor) of that zone where what you are about to place is. Only footprints that have assets in this sub-warehouse appear. If the zone has a single footprint, or the footprint a single asset, they are chosen by themselves.
relFootprint.example: in Zone 6 you choose footprint R-05 and its asset A-05 is chosen.

layoutFmtReset.what: Removes this zone's own format: it goes back to its type color.
layoutFmtReset.example: the zone no longer needs its own color and looks like the other dry zones again.

layoutZonePlanM2.what: The m² your plan states for this room. The system compares what you drew against that number and warns if they differ (more than 3%). It is optional.
layoutZonePlanM2.example: your plan says the Warehouse room is 38.89 m²; if what you drew gives 45 m², it turns amber so you can check the measures.

layoutFreeShape.what: Turns this rectangle into a free-shape zone: it is edited side by side, the way the plan shows it, for L-shaped rooms, notches or slanted walls.
layoutFreeShape.example: the Supplier dock is L-shaped: you switch it to free shape and type its 6 sides.

layoutSidesOpen.what: Shows or hides the sides of this free-shape zone so you can type or fix them.
layoutSidesOpen.example: you tap Sides and change side 3 from 1.27 to 1.30 m.

layoutSideDir.what: Which way this side goes, from the corner where the previous one ends. The diagonal arrows also ask for their tilt.
layoutSideDir.example: Right for a horizontal wall; Right and up for a wall that rises at a slant.

layoutSideTilt.what: How many degrees the side tilts from the horizontal (0.1 to 89.9). It only appears with the diagonal arrows.
layoutSideTilt.example: a wall that rises 30° to the right: you pick Right and up and type 30.

layoutSideLen.what: How long this side is, in meters, as your plan states it.
layoutSideLen.example: 4.57 for the width of the dock.

layoutSideAdd.what: Adds a side at the end. Sides are typed in order, going around the shape on the inside.

layoutSideInsert.what: Adds a side right after this one without touching the others. This side is split into two equal parts and the shape still closes; then you change which way the new part goes or how long it is.
layoutSideInsert.example: you need a notch between side 2 and side 3: you tap + on side 2 and set the new part to Down, 1 m.

layoutSideClose.what: Adds the straight sides that are missing to get back to the corner where you started.
layoutSideClose.example: you are missing 6.30 m to the left and 6.17 m up: one tap adds both sides.

layoutSideCloseLine.what: Closes the shape with a single straight side, from the last corner to the starting one, even if it ends up slanted.
layoutSideCloseLine.example: your last side runs diagonally back to where you started: you close it in one go.

layoutContornoMode.what: How you enter the outline: by sides (which way it goes and how long, as the plan shows it) or by corners (their X and Y meters).
layoutContornoMode.example: with the plan at hand you use By sides; if you already have coordinates you use By corners.

layoutObstTipo.what: What this obstacle is: Column, Level difference (a stretch of floor that is higher or lower) or Other (anything in the way). Walls are added in the Walls step.
layoutObstTipo.example: you mark the concrete post as Column and the stretch of higher floor next to the dock as Level difference.

layoutObstUbicacion.what: How you place it: On the outline (against a side of the warehouse: you pick the side, how far from the corner it starts, how long it is and how thick) or Inside the warehouse (with X, Y, length and width).
layoutObstUbicacion.example: the wall of a dock goes On the outline; a column in the middle of the warehouse goes Inside the warehouse.

layoutObstLado.what: The side of the outline the obstacle is against. The number is the same as in the sides table.
layoutObstLado.example: Side 3 is the third side you entered.

layoutObstDist.what: How many meters from the corner where the side starts the obstacle begins.
layoutObstDist.example: a wall that starts 2 m from the corner: you enter 2.

layoutObstLargo.what: How long it is. On an obstacle on the outline, empty means the whole side.
layoutObstLargo.example: you leave the length empty for a wall that covers the whole side and enter 3 for a 3 m wall.

layoutObstAlturaPared.what: How tall this wall is on side A at its starting corner (where the distance starts; for an inside wall, its top or left end), in meters and measured from the floor of that side. It is the wall's own height, not the footprints': they can be equal or different. If you leave it empty the contour's height at that point applies (or the warehouse average if it is inside), also measured from the floor of its side: a higher floor does not cut it down.
layoutObstAlturaPared.example: a wall that starts at the tallest part of the warehouse: 9 m.

layoutObstAlturaParedB.what: How tall this wall is on side B (the opposite of A), at its starting corner, in meters and measured from the floor of that side: if the zone on that side is higher, its floor rises. Leave it empty if the wall is the same height on both sides (the same height from each side's floor, even if one floor is higher); with it the wall gets a step on top, each half of its thickness at the height of its side.
layoutObstAlturaParedB.example: a wall between the warehouse (5 m on side A) and the offices, which are 1.2 m higher: on side B you enter 3 and its top is at 4.2 m.

layoutObstAlturaParedBFin.what: How tall the wall is on side B at its ending corner, in meters from the floor of that side. Empty: the same as the start of side B (or the height of side A if you did not write the start).
layoutObstAlturaParedBFin.example: side B drops from 3 m at one end to 2.5 m at the other.

layoutParedLados.what: What each side of the wall faces, calculated: the zone on that side (and its floor, if not level) or «outside» if it falls outside the building. Side A is toward the inside of the building on a contour wall; on a wall inside the building it is down on the sketch (to the left if the wall is vertical). Side B is the opposite.
layoutParedLados.example: Side A faces Warehouse and Side B faces Offices · floor +1.2 m.

layoutObstAlturaParedFin.what: How tall this wall is at its ending corner, in meters. If it differs from the start, the wall rises or drops from one corner to the other (for irregular warehouses, taller on one side than the other). Empty: the same as the start, or the contour's height at that point if you did not write the start either.
layoutObstAlturaParedFin.example: a wall that drops from 9 m at one end to 6 m at the other.

layoutObstGrosor.what: The thickness of the obstacle toward the inside of the warehouse, in meters.
layoutObstGrosor.example: a block wall is 0.2 m thick.

layoutObstAncho.what: How long the obstacle is the other way (in Y), in meters.
layoutObstAncho.example: a square column of 0.6 × 0.6 m: length 0.6 and width 0.6.

layoutObstXY.what: Where the corner of the obstacle is inside the warehouse, in meters from the origin of the Layout.
layoutObstXY.example: a column at 5 m in X and 6 m in Y.

layoutObstAltura.what: Only for the Level difference: its height above the floor, in meters. If it is lower than the floor, write it with a minus sign. The m³ of the warehouse change with it: if the floor rises, there is less air.
layoutObstAltura.example: a platform 0.3 m higher: you enter 0.3; a pit 0.5 m lower: you enter -0.5.

layoutParedTodo.what: Adds a wall to each side of the outline that does not have one yet. The ones you already have are not repeated.
layoutParedTodo.example: you mark the whole outline as wall and then remove the one of an open dock.

layoutSec_transito.what: The aisles of the warehouse: where people, forklifts, carts and platforms pass. An aisle goes inside a zone (the zone comes by itself from its place), connects with another aisle that touches it, and nothing can be inside: no footprints, columns, walls or level differences. Who passes through it is chosen from the «What Passes» catalog (Catalogs), and it has to fit (width, length and height). The code (T001, T002…) is set by the system. The aisle m² come from here.
layoutSec_transito.example: a main aisle 25 m long by 3 m wide inside Zone 1, for people and forklifts: it becomes T001.

layoutSensorZonas.what: The zones whose temperature and humidity this sensor measures. The wall is only for placing it; here you choose which zones it measures, one or several. If you choose none, it measures the zone where it is placed. In the Heat map each zone is painted with the average of the sensors that measure it.
layoutSensorZonas.example: a sensor on the wall between the Dock and Zone 1 measures both: you tick Dock and Zone 1, and both zones use its reading.

layoutTransitoQuien.what: Who passes through this aisle, chosen from the «What Passes» catalog (people, forklifts, carts, platforms, whatever models you have). You can tick several. The sizes come from the catalog; if what you tick does not fit in the aisle, it shows in red and it can't be saved.
layoutTransitoQuien.example: you tick People and Forklift on the central aisle; if it is less than 1.2 m wide, the forklift shows in red.

layoutTransitoMedidas.what: How big each thing that passes is (width, length and height, in meters). They start with default sizes and you can change them; they are used to check whether it fits in each aisle. «Other» is checked once you enter its sizes.
layoutTransitoMedidas.example: your forklift is 1.4 m wide: you change 1.2 to 1.4 and the narrower aisles show in red.

layoutTransitoAltoLibre.what: How much free space there is above this aisle, in meters. It is optional: empty means the height is not checked.
layoutTransitoAltoLibre.example: a low beam leaves 2 m free: you enter 2 and a 2.2 m tall forklift shows in red.

layoutSgConteo.what: How many safety items are in each status, using the nearest date of each one (its expiry or its next check) against today: Valid, Due soon (the warning days or fewer are left), Overdue (the date has passed) and No date.
layoutSgConteo.example: you see «Due soon · 2» and «Overdue · 1»: there are three items to take care of.

layoutSgAvisar.what: How many days ahead an item shows as «Due soon». The default is 30; it applies to all the safety items of this Layout.
layoutSgAvisar.example: with 45, an extinguisher that expires in 40 days already shows as «Due soon».

layoutSec_obstaculos.what: The things in the way in the warehouse that are not walls: columns, level differences (a stretch of floor that is higher or lower) and anything else. Each one goes on a side of the outline or inside the warehouse, with its place and sizes; a level difference also has its height. They show on the sketch and in 3D while this step is on, and nothing can go inside an aisle. The add button is at the top, next to the title.
layoutSec_obstaculos.example: a 0.6 m column in the middle of the warehouse and a 0.15 m level difference next to the dock.

layoutSec_paredes.what: The walls of the warehouse. Each one goes on a side of the outline (the whole length or just a stretch, with its thickness) or inside the warehouse, with its place and sizes. Walls go from floor to ceiling in 3D and are always drawn on the sketch. The add buttons are at the top: «Add wall» and «Wall on the whole outline».
layoutSec_paredes.example: a wall on every side of the warehouse except the open dock side, and a 12 m wall in the middle to separate the refrigerated zone.

layoutParedAgregar.what: Adds a new wall on side 1 of the outline, along its whole length; then you place it with its side, distance, length and thickness.
layoutParedAgregar.example: you add a wall and move it to side 3 with a length of 8 m.

layoutSec_seguridad.what: The safety items of the warehouse placed on the plan: fire extinguishers, hydrants, emergency doors, first-aid kits, alarms or pull stations, showers and eyewashes, assembly points and evacuation routes. Each one is a point (X and Y, in meters; a route also has its end point) with its type and its name or model. The system sets the code: each type with its own letter and count (E001, I001, P001, B001, L001, O001, U001, V001), and a number is never used again even if you delete the item. The zone comes from its place. Everything must be inside the building outline: otherwise it shows in red and can't be saved. Each item can have its expiry, how many days between checks and its next check: the status (Valid, Due soon, Overdue or No date) comes from the nearest date against today, they are counted at the top, and on the sketch those due soon get an amber ring and the overdue ones a red ring. This does not block saving. They show on the sketch, in 3D, on the public QR page and on the downloaded sheet while this step is on.
layoutSec_seguridad.example: a 6 kg dry-chemical extinguisher at 5 m in X and 5 m in Y (E001), the west exit emergency door on the left side of the building (P001) and an evacuation route running from the central aisle to that door (V001).

layoutSec_objetos.what: The people and forklifts drawn on the plan, to scale, as a still picture of how the warehouse is (it does not follow anyone live). Each one has its place (X and Y are its center, in meters), where it faces (turn in degrees) and its equipment or person, chosen from the «What Passes» catalog: its drawing and sizes come from there, and if they change in the catalog they change here. They show on the sketch and in 3D while this step is on.
layoutSec_objetos.example: a forklift in the central aisle, 12 m in X and 9.5 m in Y, facing right (turn 0), and a person next to it.

layoutObjetoAgregar.what: Adds an object at the center of the warehouse: it starts as a person, with its default sizes. In «Equipment or person» you choose whether it is a forklift, a cart or a platform, and then you place it with X, Y and Turn.
layoutObjetoAgregar.example: you add one, choose Forklift in «Equipment or person» and move it to the aisle where it works.

layoutOrigin.what: Where on the map the first corner is; the sides are drawn from there.

layoutCanvas.what: The map of the warehouse, drawn by itself from the data you enter: walls, zones, racks, doors and power connections. When you touch a line of Zones, Footprint-Space, Assets or Positions, what that line is gets highlighted here with a thin, dotted, rotating outline (so the measures and how close it is to the rest stay visible) and the line stays marked in the table; for a position its rack is marked and the level and column are written. If you touch the shape on the map (without dragging it), it is highlighted with the thick orange outline and its line is marked; touch it again to go back to the dotted one. In 3D, the line you choose is also marked with an orange outline around its shape, and the mark goes away when you change step.
layoutCanvas.example: you change the width of a zone and the map updates instantly; you touch line R-03 and rack R-03 is marked with its dotted outline; you touch the rack on the map and it is marked thick so you can find it at a glance.

layoutSave.what: Saves the Layout with all the changes. Until you save, only you can see them.
layoutSave.example: you finish entering the doors and save so others can see the Layout.

layoutDiscard.what: Undoes the changes you have not saved and goes back to the last saved Layout.
layoutDiscard.example: you entered something by mistake and go back to how it was.

layoutSummary.what: A summary of each zone: its name and its zone type (each in its own column), its m², how many spaces it has, how much floor they take and how many storage m³ there are.
layoutSummary.example: you see that Zone A is 25% occupied by its racks.

layoutPlanWidth.what: The real width of the plan, in meters. With it the system knows the scale to draw your warehouse over the plan.
layoutPlanWidth.example: the plan is 48 meters wide and you type it in.

layoutQrMenu.what: Downloads the Layout sheet with the map and the QR, or copies the QR link. The QR never changes and always opens the latest saved Layout.
layoutQrMenu.example: you download the sheet, print it and stick it at the warehouse entrance.

layoutQrPdf.what: Opens the window to download the sheet as a PDF: there you choose the size (A3, A4, Letter, Half letter, Card or any width and length in cm), see how it will look and download it with the map, the KPIs and the QR, ready to print. The sheet comes out as you see the sketch: if you hid the measures or left only some steps active (doors, power, zones...), it only has that. It has what was last saved.
layoutQrPdf.example: you leave only Zones active, hide the measures and the sheet comes out with only the zones, no doors or measures.

layoutQrPng.what: Opens the same window to download the sheet as an image, at the size you choose, to send by message or email. It comes out as you see the sketch (same layers and measures). It has what was last saved.
layoutQrPng.example: you send it by message to a supervisor.

layoutQrLink.what: Copies the address the QR carries, in case you need it somewhere it will not be printed.
layoutQrLink.example: you paste it in an email so it can be opened from a phone.

layoutQrRegen.what: Replaces the QR with a new one. The old one stops working and the sheets have to be printed again. Use it only if the QR left the company.
layoutQrRegen.example: someone photographed the QR outside the warehouse and you prefer to cancel it.

sidebarFlyoutSection.what: This is the name of the section you hovered over. Its options unfold once you reach it; a click opens the sidebar with the section expanded.
sidebarFlyoutSection.example: with the sidebar closed you hover the Customer Service icon, reach its name and pick Our Customers without opening the sidebar.

genericActions.what: This is where the buttons to edit, delete, or do something else with this record live.
genericActions.example: you tap the pencil icon in this column to edit that row.

genericUsername.what: The username this person uses to log in to the system.
genericUsername.example: "admin_saas" is what that person types on the login screen, along with their password.

genericEmail.what: The email address registered for this account.
genericEmail.example: the system uses this email if this person needs to recover their access.

genericCreatedAt.what: The date this record was created.
genericCreatedAt.example: you see how long this account or record has existed in the system.

genericStatus.what: Says what state this record is in right now (for example, Active or Inactive).
genericStatus.example: you see at a glance whether this account is still active, without opening it.

genericName.what: The name that identifies this record.
genericName.example: you see the name this row is known by in the list.

createNewRecord.what: Creates a new record for this list, ready to fill in.
createNewRecord.example: you tap this button to add a new client, item, or record to the list.

genericColumnHeader.what: This column shows "{name}" for every record. Click the title to sort the table by it, drag it to move the column, and use the funnel to filter by this column.
genericColumnHeader.example: to find a record quickly, filter "{name}" by typing part of its value.

genericColumnCell.what: This is the "{name}" of this record.

savedLayout.what: Opens your list of saved layouts: pick one and the table rearranges instantly, or add a new one. While one is applied, its name is written on this icon.
savedLayout.example: you save "Supervisors view" with only the columns you use and apply it every morning with one click.

savedSearch.what: Opens your list of saved searches: pick one and the table filters instantly, or add a new one by choosing the columns and their filters. While one is applied, its name is written on this icon.
savedSearch.example: you save "Active this month" and apply it every morning with one click.

filterToggle.what: Opens or closes the filter panel above the table, to look for records by several fields at once.
filterToggle.example: you open the panel, pick a Status, tap Search and see only those records.

filterClear.what: Clears every filter and leaves the table as it started: all records and the columns in their original order.
filterClear.example: after searching for one client, you tap Clear to see everyone again.

filterSigns.what: Types the search signs with one tap: $ asks for another word BEFORE the searched one, @ another word AFTER it, and the comma separates searches (either one matches). You can also type them. With Starts with only @ works, and with Equal to only the comma.
filterSigns.example: you type "rack", tap $ and type "drawer": "rack$drawer" finds the texts where "drawer" comes before "rack".

clearSearch.what: Removes the saved search you have applied and leaves the table with no filters, showing every record.
clearSearch.example: you applied "Active this month" and want to see everything again: tap the ✕.

filterAdvanced.what: Adds more filters to the panel: pick any column of the table and its field shows up here to filter by. You can keep going until every column is included; the ones you add are remembered for this table.
filterAdvanced.example: you want to filter by Contracted Cost besides Plan: tap Advanced filter and pick that column.

filterPanelClear.what: Removes everything filtered, in the panel fields and in the columns, and shows every record again. It does not change the column layout.
filterPanelClear.example: you checked the active clients and want to see them all again.

filterPanelField.what: Filters the table by this column. It applies when you tap Search, like the other panel fields, and it is the same filter as the column header.
filterPanelField.example: you pick the Basic and Professional plans and tap Search.

clearLayout.what: Removes the saved layout you have applied and returns the table to its default layout: the one assigned to you, or the table's original if you have none.
clearLayout.example: you applied "Supervisors view" and want things back as they were: tap the ✕.
